content.comment_body: I have a simple application monitoring digital inputs on [product_name], and I want to save the date and time whenever an input is activated. It works fine while the device is powered on; the data log is saved to EEPROM, and I can use [product_name] programming software to download the log or remove the SD card to access the data. However, if there are input triggers and a power outage occurs, I lose the data log for those events. Is there a way to have [product_name] automatically save the log to the SD card each time an input is triggered?

No, there is no way to do this directly with [product_name]. You could consider using a backup battery or undervoltage power supply to maintain voltage in case of mains failure, allowing the device to continue operating.
That's what I suspected. Thanks regardless.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face data loss when using the datalog feature of [product_name] due to power outages. Data is typically saved only during explicit export or session end, causing unsaved triggered data to be lost during unexpected shutdowns. Users seek an automated solution for immediate log saving to SD card upon each input trigger.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to automatically save the datalog to the SD card every time an input is triggered, minimizing data loss during unexpected power interruptions.
